page.layout: One column of running text. Above it, the running head and page number. Within the text, an italic Latin epigram set as an indented block of verse. Below it, a French paragraph and an italic attribution line. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: dix-huict & dix-neuf ans. Il y a cent ans
que Iulius Cesar Scaliger, grand & subtil
Philosophe, aussi bien que tres-sçauant & tres-excellent
Medecin, demeurant à Agen, ville de
Guyenne, que vous auez appellé vous-mesme
de l'ignorance des nouueaux Docteurs de
Montpelier : c'est en ses Poësies Latines,
Epiderpidum lib. 3. Le titre de l'Epigramme
est, Ignari Medici, aux Ignorans Medecins.

l.i: Statim ubi tetigit vel pede Pessuli tabernas,
Et duas modulo, & ordine formulas docentum
Olfecit, ab his illico temeraria regnū,
Quantum Pharicus Perfica iam castra sequutus
Clamauit ad Istrum, neque Stentorive cedunt

main_text.l: Par vn autre Epigramme addressé à l'Es-
chole de Montpelier, il descrit la friponne-
rie d'vn Medecin de Montpelier, que l'Escho-
le souftenoit & approuoit pour sien. C'est

l.i: en la page 639. ad Montem Pessulum d' Caluo.
Iean Hucher, natif de Bonnieres prés de Beaunais

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "Perfica" is printed as shown and may be a printing error for "Persica"; kept as printed. "sessione" is read from a long-s form. The italic/roman boundary in the French sentence ending "en la page 639. ad Montem Pessulum d' Caluo." is uncertain. Small dash-like marks in the left margin beside the verses are not printed text and are omitted. The small mark at the foot centre is not text and is omitted.
